source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: As the clock ticked relentlessly, the emergency room buzzed with activity. Nurses hurriedly navigated the tangle of corridors, flitting back and forth between the patient bays. A bedraggled couple sat in the waiting chairs, glancing anxiously from their companion to the door. Their complaint was clear: they were growing increasingly agitated by the length of their wait. Beside them, a patient lay in distress, his chest heaving, a wristband secured around his forearm. Next to the bed, a nurse typed furiously at the computer, her brows furrowed in concentration as she filled out forms and pages of intercom requests blared overhead. The orderly treaded purposefully, carting medical supplies and equipment, pausing only to brief the nurse before resuming his brisk pace. The register of clinical urgency whirred, its lights blinking urgently, reminders of the constant stream of critical cases. Meanwhile, the waiting companion watched, restless, their eyes darting towards the entrance, hoping against hope that relief would come soon.
